answers.falsifier: an AST scan of bin/proofs/test_*.py finds no list literal whose first element is the string bash ; an AST scan finds no argv headed by str(CAIRN), a direct exec of the bin/cairn shebang script
answers.how: Edit the four proofs: script paths go through cairn.tools.base.script_argv.bash_script_argv, -c and --rcfile commands use a module _BASH that is shutil.which('bash') on nt and 'bash' elsewhere. Add bin/proofs/test_no_bin_proof_spawns_a_bare_bash.py, an AST scan of bin/proofs/test_*.py for list literals whose first element is the string bash and for str(CAIRN) as an argv head. No change to bin/cairn. Other reds in those four proofs (census of 1342 commands, a FileExistsError, a 201-vs-10 line trim) are other causes, measured at baseline, and are left alone.
answers.title: bin's proofs run the host's bash and never exec bin/cairn as a Windows program
answers.traces_to: Law 3 and Law 8: a proof that runs another OS's shell on a box measures that shell, not the component; Law 4: held by a scan, not remembered.
answers.what: Every bin proof builds its bash argv from the host's bash (shutil.which on Windows) or from bash_script_argv, and none spawns the bare word bash or execs bin/cairn directly; an AST door proof over bin/proofs holds it.
